enhanced.fullText:
The Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (ADA), codified at 42 U.S.C. §§ 12101-12213, represents landmark civil rights legislation that prohibits discrimination against individuals with disabilities across multiple sectors, including higher education institutions. Title II of the ADA (42 U.S.C. § 12131-12165) specifically governs public colleges and universities as public entities, while Title III (42 U.S.C. § 12181-12189) applies to private institutions that serve as places of public accommodation.

Under 42 U.S.C. § 12132, public universities must ensure that "no qualified individual with a disability shall, by reason of such disability, be excluded from participation in or be denied the benefits of the services, programs, or activities of a public entity, or be subjected to discrimination by any such entity." The implementing regulations at 28 CFR Part 35 require institutions to provide reasonable modifications to policies, practices, and procedures when necessary to avoid discrimination, unless such modifications would fundamentally alter the nature of the service, program, or activity.

Higher education institutions must provide auxiliary aids and services under 28 CFR § 35.160, including interpreters, assistive listening devices, note-takers, written materials in alternative formats, and accessible electronic and information technology. The 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design, incorporated by reference in 28 CFR § 35.104, establish specific architectural accessibility requirements for campus facilities, including classrooms, libraries, dining facilities, and residence halls.

The ADA Amendments Act of 2008 (Pub. L. 110-325) significantly broadened the definition of disability under 42 U.S.C. § 12102, emphasizing that the definition should be construed broadly and that the primary focus should be on whether discrimination occurred rather than whether an individual has a covered disability. This expansion has increased the number of students eligible for accommodations in higher education settings.

Enforcement occurs through multiple federal agencies: the Department of Justice handles structural compliance under Title II, the Department of Education's Office for Civil Rights investigates discrimination complaints, and the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission addresses employment-related violations under Title I. Private individuals may file lawsuits under 42 U.S.C. § 12133, seeking injunctive relief and attorney's fees under 42 U.S.C. § 12205. Violations can result in termination of federal funding, monetary damages, and court-ordered remedial measures.

Institutions must designate an ADA coordinator under 28 CFR § 35.107, establish grievance procedures per 28 CFR § 35.107(b), and conduct self-evaluations of current services and policies under 28 CFR § 35.105. The regulation requires proactive measures including transition plans for structural modifications and ongoing accessibility assessments of academic programs, student services, and campus activities.
enhanced.summary: The ADA mandates that higher education institutions provide equal access to programs and services for students with disabilities through reasonable accommodations, auxiliary aids, and barrier-free facilities, with enforcement by DOJ, ED, and EEOC.
enhanced.requirements:
## Accommodation Services
- Establish disability services office with qualified personnel
- Provide reasonable modifications to academic policies and procedures per 28 CFR § 35.130
- Supply auxiliary aids including interpreters, alternative format materials, and assistive technology
- Conduct interactive process to determine appropriate accommodations

## Physical Accessibility
- Ensure campus facilities comply with 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design
- Maintain accessible routes to all programs and services per 28 CFR § 35.150
- Provide accessible parking, restrooms, and emergency evacuation procedures

## Administrative Compliance
- Designate ADA coordinator under 28 CFR § 35.107
- Establish formal grievance procedures for disability-related complaints
- Conduct comprehensive self-evaluation of policies and programs per 28 CFR § 35.105
- Develop transition plan for structural accessibility improvements

## Program Access
- Ensure all academic programs are accessible to qualified students with disabilities
- Provide equal access to housing, dining, transportation, and student activities
- Train faculty and staff on ADA compliance and accommodation procedures
enhanced.reportingRequirements: No specific federal reporting deadlines required. Institutions must maintain accommodation records, grievance files, and self-evaluation documentation. Submit compliance data upon request during OCR investigations or DOJ reviews. Report significant accessibility barriers and remediation timelines in transition plans updated as needed.
